findings.location: Paragraph 1 (sentence: "He was intent on locating Brother Silas before the service began.")
findings.source_quote: he would crane his neck in search of the hoary head of the fellowship’s oldest member
findings.suggested_fix: Translate "the hoary head" to convey "white-haired/elder" (not "upweke" which means "lonely"). For example: "aliweka shingo kutafuta kichwa chake chelewe kilicho na nywele za kijivu cha mwanachama mzee wa kikundi" or more smoothly "aliweka shingo kutafuta nywele zake za kijivu — mzee zaidi katika kikundi." Preserve meaning that it refers to an old/white-haired member.
findings.translation_quote: algekea shingo yake kutafuta kichwa cha upweke cha mwanachama mzee wa kikundi

findings.source_quote: A glass jar spilling wrapped mints beside a potted plant
findings.suggested_fix: Use a Kiswahili word for "potted plant" that is not a cooking vessel. For example: "chupa ya glasi ikimwaga mints zilizofungwa kando ya mmea uliopandwa kwenye bakuli/katoni/utepe" or "...kando ya mmea uliowekwa kwenye chombo". Also consider translating "wrapped mints" as "mints zilizofunikwa" or "zimetengenezwa" more naturally.
findings.translation_quote: Chupa ya glasi ikimwaga mints iliyofungwa kando ya mmea kwenye sufuria

findings.suggested_fix: Consider a more natural Kiswahili rendering. "Mtu wa Mints" is understandable but awkward. Alternatives: "Mwanaume wa Mints", "Mtu wa Mints wa Kanisa", or a descriptive title such as "Mwanaume wa Mints (Mtu wa Mints)". If you wish to preserve a concise title, "Mwanaume wa Mints" is preferable.
